description: 32x24 RGB/8; a layer mask whose rect strictly contains the layer rect (mask 24x20 at (4,2), layer 14x12 at (8,6)).

provenance.author: Christian Budde <christian.wilhelm.budde@meko.de>
provenance.licenseNote: Self-authored from scratch; no third-party artwork; CC0-1.0 for redistribution in this repository.

expectationSource.method: psd-tools PSDImage.open() for structure and layer records; composite() for compositePixels; layer.numpy() for layerPixels. No Agogo code in the loop.

externalVerification.notes: tools/psdfixtures/verify_dump.py re-read the Agogo re-export with psd-tools 1.19.0; the file was accepted and reported the expected structure. ImageMagick was not installed in this environment, so this row rests on one independent reader rather than two. See testdata/VERIFICATION.md. The layer keeps its own (8,6) 14x12 bounds and the oversized mask still attenuates it; only the stored mask rect and default fill are widened.

writer.lossyReason: PLAN.md S.10.2: psdexport emits layer channels in its own fixed order (0,1,2,-1; gray 0,-1) and always emits an alpha channel, because the engine model is RGBA. This fixture was authored with alpha first (-1,0,1,2), so every re-exported record's channelIds differ in order. The PSD spec does not prescribe channel order and readers key on the ID, so this is a spelling difference rather than lost data. Allowlisting a path suppresses the WHOLE assertion, so this entry on its own would also excuse a dropped -2 user mask or a corrupted ID; it does not, because the ID set is asserted separately at psdRecords[N].channelIds.preserved, which is emitted strictly and which no writer.lossy entry can reach. That path permits exactly one gained channel, the alpha psdexport always writes, and nothing else. psd-tools 1.19.0 reads the re-export correctly; ImageMagick was not installed in this environment, so this fixture rests on one independent reader rather than two (see testdata/VERIFICATION.md). PLAN.md S.10.4: psdimport rasterizes the layer mask into a document-sized buffer and discards the mask rectangle and its default fill, so the re-export stores a full-canvas mask.rect with defaultFill 255 instead of the original rect and fill. The mask still attenuates exactly the same pixels - the discarded default fill is folded into the rasterized mask - so only the stored extent and fill byte differ, not the coverage.
